Angiotensin I and II is a key component of the Renin-Angiotensin-System (RAS). Angiotensin I is converted to Angiotensin II by ACE (Angiotensin Converting Enzyme). Angiotensin II is a potent vasocontractor and therefore blocks by ACE-I. Another effect of angiotensin II is that it stimulates aldosterone secretion from the adrenal cortex. Aldosterone is a hormone that promotes the absorption of sodium and water in the kidneys, which can lead to hypertension. Therefore, by preventing the formation of angiotensin II, ACE-I's have a blood pressure lowering effect.  Other drugs that may be used to treat hypertension include:Thiazide diureticsBeta blockersCalcium channel blockers

The lateral corticospinal tract is the only motor pathway that originates in the cerebral cortex (the other descending pathways originate in the motor nuclei of the medulla). It is the only pathway that provides highly discriminative control over voluntary rapid and dexterous movements of the individual joints and digits of the extremities.  The anterior corticospinal tract controls non-stereotyped movements of the axial muscles.  The rubrospinal tract originates in the red nucleus of the midbrain and provides non-discriminative control over muscle tone and gross movements of the limbs.  The vestibulospinal tract originates in the vestibular nuclei of the medullach controls balance and posture by providing non-discriminative control over extensor muscles of the axial skeleton.  The tectospinal tract originates in the upper tectum of the midbrain and controls orienting of the head in response to visual and auditory stimuli.

Answer A is incorrect - the sodium potassium pump is responsible for maintaining the resting potential, if this ceased to work then there would be no further action potentials as the membrane potential would be at 0mV.  Answer B is incorrect - inactivation of potassium ion voltage gated channel would mean that there is no outward flow of potassium during repolarisation, the cell would fail to repolarise and t become non excitable.  Answer C is correct - during the slow/prolonged depolarization of accommodation, sodium ions are trapped in the hydrated state, they cannot conduct an action potential, the cell fails to repolarise and the threshold potential increases.  Answer D is incorrect - activation of potassium voltage gated channel would mean that there is an increased outward flow of potassium during repolarisation, the cell would repolarise too quickly and the threshold potential would increase.  Answer E is incorrect - activation of Calcium ion voltage gated channel would mean that there is an increased inward flow of calcium during repolarisation, the cell would fail to repolarise and t become non excitable.
